newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait yet to decide on OPEC quota rise-minister.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait yet to decide on OPEC quota rise-minister.

text.p: Kuwait's oil minister said on Wednesday his country would decide whether it would seek an OPEC output quota rise after reviewing reports that would be presented at the organisation's June 25 ministerial meeting.

"There are some reports that would be submited to their excellencies the (OPEC oil) ministers...in the light of those studies and proposals we would be able to decide," Isa al-Mazeedi told Reuters in a brief interview.
In May, OPEC President Libyan Oil Minister Abdullah Salem al-Badri said he expected the group to keep its 25.03 million barrels per day (bpd) output ceiling in the June 25 meeting.
Kuwait, which puts its production capacity at 2.5 million bpd, has often said if OPEC decides to increase its output ceiling it would seek to increase its two million bpd quota by about 200,000 bpd.
Oil prices were "satisfactory at present", said Mazeedi. But, "We hope, God willing, to see better indictors in the soon future."
Oil prices suggested that OPEC countries were complying with their quotas, he said.

However, "OPEC members do not wish to see any violations in the quotas allocated to (member) countries, therefore, we would like to stress that this issue would tackled in the coming meeting," he said.
Independent assessments put the production of OPEC countries at more than 27 million bpd compared to the agreed ceiling of 25.03 million bpd.
